VidAngel Review: How It Works, Our Experience & Current Deal

Our Honest VidAngel Review After Years of Using It

We’ve used VidAngel for years and it has made watching TV a much more pleasant experience. Even shows you’d expect to be “safe” can surprise you. VidAngel lets me filter out language, explicit scenes, violence, and other moments I simply don’t want my family or myself to see or hear. Because of this, I can watch far more of the movies and buzz-worthy shows everyone is talking about without all the extras I don’t want. I also get more value from the streaming services I’m already paying for because there are fewer shows I have to skip entirely. It has been a total game changer for family movie night, the kids watching on their own, and my own watch list. 🙌

Streaming has made it incredibly easy to find something to watch. My daughter was actually horrified when she learned that TV used to mean “only repeats in the summer” and racing back from the other room when the commercial break ended because if you missed it, you missed it!

But there is one thing I miss about those days: TV felt a lot easier to make family-friendly. Now, plenty of really good movies and shows include nudity, sexual content, profanity, graphic violence, disturbing scenes, and other content we just don’t want to see or hear.

And sometimes it’s the show you don’t expect that catches you off guard. That’s one of the biggest reasons I still use VidAngel after all these years. I don’t want to sit with the remote in my hand wishing I could have muted something or fast-forwarded through a scene.

That’s where VidAngel comes in. Below I’ll show you how VidAngel works, which streaming services and devices it supports, popular shows worth checking out, and the features we’ve found most useful.

What Is VidAngel?

VidAngel is a streaming filtering service that works with supported movies and TV shows from streaming services you already pay for.

Instead of replacing Netflix, Prime Video, Apple TV+, or your other subscriptions, VidAngel connects to supported services and lets you choose what you want automatically muted or skipped.

You can choose filters for things like language, intimacy and sexual content, nudity, violence, substances, disturbing content, and more.

The important part is that you decide what you want filtered. What bothers one family may be completely different from what bothers another.

VidAngel also offers select licensed family-friendly content, including titles associated with Angel Studios such as The Wingfeather Saga, Freelancers, and select Dry Bar Comedy specials. I absolutely love Dry Bar for clean laughs!

One important distinction: VidAngel does not automatically make every movie appropriate for children. Some mature themes, storylines, or disturbing ideas may remain even after filtering. I still recommend checking the title and choosing filters based on who’s watching.

How Does VidAngel Work?

Whether it’s a movie or a TV show, VidAngel gives you control over what you see and hear.

Filter options can include:

  • Profanity and specific types of language
  • Sexual content and intimacy
  • Nudity
  • Violence and gore
  • Disturbing images
  • Drug and alcohol use
  • Blasphemy
  • Other show-specific content

Language filters generally mute the audio when an unwanted word or phrase occurs, while visual filters skip the selected portion of a scene.

The filtering happens automatically while you’re watching, which is SO much better than trying to predict when you need to grab the remote.

You can also customize filters for individual shows. Maybe I don’t mind the action in a particular movie but don’t want the language. Or maybe I’m watching something with my kids and want significantly more filtering than I would use on my own.

That’s what makes VidAngel different from simply relying on a TV or movie rating.

Popular Shows to Watch with VidAngel

This is one of my favorite things about VidAngel: it opens up shows I might otherwise decide aren’t worth watching because of the language, violence, or explicit scenes.

If you’re wondering what to watch with VidAngel, these are some popular titles worth searching for:

  • Bridgerton – Enjoy the romance, costumes, family drama, and story while filtering sexual content, nudity, and other content you’d rather skip.
  • Reacher – A popular action thriller for viewers who want more control over profanity, violence, and mature content.
  • Lioness – A CIA thriller with plenty of action, suspense, and mature material that viewers may want to filter.
  • Outer Banks – Treasure hunts, mystery, and drama, with options to filter language, violence, and other mature elements in supported episodes.
  • Yellowstone – A compelling family and ranch drama with strong language, violence, and sexual content that many viewers prefer to filter.
  • Landman – Another Taylor Sheridan drama with an interesting cast and story, along with plenty of mature content.
  • The Night Agent – A fast-moving conspiracy thriller for viewers who enjoy suspense but want more control over what appears on screen.
  • Outlander – A historical romance and drama with explicit content that can make filtering especially appealing.
  • Stranger Things – A supernatural mystery series where some viewers prefer to reduce graphic violence, disturbing imagery, and strong language.

Important: VidAngel does not filter every title on every streaming service. Availability changes, and filters are created for individual movies, seasons, and episodes. Always search VidAngel for the specific title you want to watch.

How to Filter Bridgerton: Can You Skip the Sex Scenes?

If you’ve wondered how to watch Bridgerton without the sex scenes, VidAngel is a great example of why filtering is useful.

For supported episodes of Bridgerton, you can connect your Netflix account, open the show in VidAngel, and select filters for sexual content, nudity, language, and other categories.

That means you can enjoy the gorgeous costumes, romance, family drama, and all the things people are talking about without having to manually fast-forward through every explicit scene.

Here’s how to get started:

  1. Connect your Netflix account to VidAngel.
  2. Search for Bridgerton in VidAngel.
  3. Choose the season and episode you want to watch.
  4. Open the available filters and select the content you want skipped or muted.
  5. Start watching through VidAngel.

Keep in mind that filtering explicit scenes does not remove every mature theme or storyline from the show.

That’s exactly what I mean when I say VidAngel has allowed me to watch so many more of the shows everyone else is talking about. I don’t necessarily want to skip the show. I just want to skip certain parts of it!

Holiday Viewing: One Remote, Three Generations, and Grandma on the Couch

Holiday movie nights are one of those times when I especially appreciate VidAngel.

Grandma picked the movie. Nobody checked the rating. Everyone is sitting together in the living room, and suddenly you’re hoping nothing awkward happens on screen.

We’ve all been there!

With VidAngel, I can choose our filters ahead of time and spend more time enjoying the movie instead of worrying about what might pop up next.

And if your family enjoys faith-based shows, The Chosen Season 6 is another timely title to look into this holiday season. The new season premiered on Prime Video in November 2026, with additional episodes rolling out through early December.

Note: Check VidAngel directly to see whether filters are available for the specific episodes of The Chosen you want to watch. Availability on Prime Video does not automatically mean a title is filterable through VidAngel.

VidAngel Parental Controls: Lock the Filters You Don’t Want Changed

This is a really useful feature for families. VidAngel now offers Parental Controls with locked filters.

You can choose the filters you want locked across your account and protect them with a parental passcode.

Those locked filters apply across profiles and can’t simply be changed by a child who decides they’d rather turn one off.

This is different from regular Default Filters. Default Filters make watching more convenient, while Parental Controls are designed to keep selected filters locked.

If your kids ever use VidAngel without you sitting next to them, this is a feature worth setting up.

Check VidAngel Content Guides Before You Watch

Another feature I really like is VidAngel Content Guides.

Instead of relying only on a vague TV rating, these guides help you understand what is actually in a movie or show before you commit to watching it.

The guides can include a visual overview of available filters, information about the show, and themes, tones, or potentially sensitive storylines.

VidAngel has published Content Guides for popular titles including Bridgerton, Outlander, and Reacher.

For me, this solves another part of the streaming problem: I want to know what I’m getting into before I press play.

A TV-MA or TV-14 rating doesn’t necessarily tell me which part of the content earned that rating or whether it’s something I personally care about.

Can’t Find a Show? Use VidAngel’s Request Portal

If the movie or show you want isn’t available to filter, VidAngel has an improved Request Portal.

In the past, you could request a title but didn’t really know what happened afterward. Now you can follow the status of your request.

  • Received – VidAngel received your request.
  • In Progress – Their team is working on it.
  • Completed – The title is available for filtering.
  • Blocked – VidAngel is unable to provide filters for that title.

You can also receive updates as the request moves through the process. That’s a big improvement over submitting a request and wondering whether anyone ever saw it.

Another handy feature: VidAngel has added search by actor. If you can’t remember the name of the movie but know who’s in it, you have another way to find what you’re looking for.

There are some titles VidAngel cannot filter because of licensing or legal restrictions. Under its current agreements, VidAngel says it cannot filter content from Disney, Lucasfilm, Warner Bros., 20th Century Fox, and their subsidiaries. So if a requested title is blocked, that may be why.

What Streaming Services Work with VidAngel?

The screenshot above shows an earlier version of VidAngel’s streaming service selection. Available services and the app interface may change.

VidAngel works with select titles from these streaming services:

  • Apple TV+
  • Netflix
  • Paramount+
  • Peacock
  • Amazon Prime Video, including eligible rentals, purchases, and subscription titles
  • Supported Amazon Add-on Channels:
    • AMC+
    • BritBox
    • Hallmark+
    • MGM+
    • Paramount+
    • PBS Masterpiece
    • STARZ

Important: VidAngel doesn’t replace these subscriptions. You need an active subscription or access to the title through the supported streaming service, then connect that service to VidAngel.

Some add-on channels must be subscribed to through Amazon Prime Video rather than directly through the channel’s standalone app.

Also, not every title from a supported service can automatically be filtered. VidAngel creates filters for individual movies and shows and continues adding new titles.

Set Up Default Filters

Within your VidAngel account, you can set Default Filters for the things you normally don’t want to see or hear.

Default Filters are profile-specific and apply automatically to new titles you start watching. You can still adjust the filters for an individual movie or episode when you want something different.

I love this because I don’t want to go through a giant filter list every single time we start something new. Set your normal preferences once, then customize when needed.

For families with children, I recommend using Default Filters for convenience and Parental Controls for filters you don’t want children to be able to change.

VidAngel Supported Devices

You can use VidAngel on:

  • Apple TV
  • Roku
  • Google and Android TV devices
  • Fire TV and compatible Fire TV Stick devices
  • iPhone and iPad
  • Android phones and tablets
  • Computers through the VidAngel website

Device compatibility note: Not every device or operating system is supported. For example, the Fire TV Stick 4K Select running Vega OS has been excluded from VidAngel support. Check VidAngel’s current device requirements before buying hardware specifically to use with the service.

What about streaming plans with ads? Compatibility varies by device and service. Ad-supported plans are not supported when using VidAngel on Roku or while casting.

Can You Cast VidAngel to Your TV?

Yes. Using the VidAngel mobile app, you can cast to compatible TVs with:

  • Chromecast or TVs with Chromecast built in
  • AirPlay to compatible AirPlay 2-enabled devices

If you have trouble connecting, check that your streaming subscription, VidAngel app, and casting device are all compatible.

Choose the subscription that works best for you and follow the account setup instructions.

When you choose a title, you can review:

  • Information about the movie or show
  • The filters available for that title
  • Which filters you currently have turned on
  • Where the title is available to stream

You can then turn individual filters on or off based on exactly what you want to see or hear.

Each movie and show has different filter options. Some scenes may be shortened or skipped entirely depending on the filters you select.

Frequently Asked Questions About VidAngel

Does VidAngel work with Netflix?

Yes. VidAngel supports filtering select Netflix movies and shows. You need an active compatible Netflix subscription, and the specific title must have VidAngel filters available.

Can VidAngel remove sex scenes from movies and TV shows?

Yes. For supported titles, VidAngel lets you choose filters that skip nudity, sexual content, and intimate scenes. Available filters vary by title, and mature themes may still remain in the story.

Does VidAngel work with Disney+, Hulu, or Max?

VidAngel does not directly support every streaming service. Disney+, Hulu, and Max are not part of the supported direct-service list above. Some titles may also be restricted because of licensing agreements.

Is VidAngel worth it if I already have Netflix or Prime Video?

For us, yes! VidAngel doesn’t replace those services, but it lets us enjoy more of the eligible movies and shows we’re already paying to access. If you frequently skip shows because of profanity, nudity, or violence, it’s worth considering.

VidAngel Review: Is VidAngel Worth It?

After using VidAngel for years, yes, I still think VidAngel is worth it—especially if there are movies and shows you want to watch but keep skipping because of explicit scenes, profanity, violence, or other content.

For me, this isn’t just about making TV more family-friendly. I use VidAngel for my own watch list, too.

There are plenty of popular shows with great stories that I genuinely want to watch. I simply don’t want every single thing the producers decided to put in them.

And that may be the biggest reason we’ve kept VidAngel for so long: watching TV is simply more pleasant.

I’m not bracing for the next scene, grabbing for the remote, or abandoning an otherwise good series. I choose what I don’t want, VidAngel handles it, and I can actually enjoy the show.

I also really like the direction VidAngel is going with features like Parental Controls, Content Guides, the improved Request Portal, and actor search. Those make it easier not only to filter what you’re watching, but to decide what to watch in the first place.

If you’re already paying for Netflix, Prime Video, Peacock, Paramount+, Apple TV+, or supported Amazon channels but avoiding a lot of their content, VidAngel can help you get more value out of subscriptions you’re already paying for.

Bottom line: If you’ve ever said, “I’d watch that if it weren’t for all the language,” “I really want to watch that, but I don’t want the sex scenes,” or “I wish there were a clean version of this show,” VidAngel is absolutely worth trying.
